source_text: Οὓς οὐδὲ ῥᾴδιον ἐκκλῖναι, οὐδὲ τὴν ἀπ' αὐτῶν φυλάξασθαι βλάβην, διὰ τὸ ἐν τῷ προσχήματι τῆς φιλίας βαθέως κατεσκευασμένην τὴν πονηρίαν κατακε κρύφθαι. Τὰ τοιαῦτα ἤθη λύκους ἅρπαγας ὀνομάζει ὁ Κύριος, ἐν ἐνδύμασι προβάτων προφαινομένους. Φεῦγε τὸ παντοδαπὸν καὶ πολλαπλοῦν τοῦ τρόπου· δίωκε δὲ ἀλήθειαν, εἰλικρίνειαν, ἁπλότητα. Ὁ ὄφις ποικίλος· διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ἕρπειν κατεδικάσθη. Ὁ δίκαιος ἄπλαστος, ὁποῖος ὁ Ἰακώβ. Διὰ τοῦτο Κατοικίζει Κύριος μονοτρόπους ἐν οἴκῳ. Αὕτη ἡ θάλασσα ἡ μεγάλη καὶ εὐρύχωρος· ἐκεῖ ἑρπετὰ, ὧν οὐκ ἔστιν ἀριθμός· ζῷα μικρὰ μετὰ μεγάλων. Ἀλλ' ὅμως σοφή τίς ἐστι παρ' αὐτοῖς καὶ εὔτακτος διακόσμησις. Οὐ γὰρ μόνον κατηγορεῖν ἔχομεν τῶν ἰχθύων, ἀλλ' ἔστιν ἃ καὶ μιμήσασθαι ἄξιον. Πῶς τὰ γένη τῶν ἰχθύων ἕκαστα τὴν ἐπιτηδείαν ἑαυτοῖς διανειμάμενα χώραν, οὐκ ἐπεμβαίνει ἀλλήλοις, ἀλλὰ τοῖς οἰκείοις ὅροις ἐνδιατρίβει; Οὐδεὶς γεωμέτρης παρ' αὐτοῖς κατένειμε τὰς οἰκήσεις· οὐ τείχεσι περιγέγραπται· οὐχ ὁροθεσίοις διῄρηται· καὶ αὐτομάτως ἑκάστῳ τὸ χρήσιμον ἀποτέτακται. Οὗτος μὲν γὰρ ὁ κόλπος τάδε τινὰ γένη τῶν ἰχθύων βόσκει, κἀκεῖνος ἕτερα· καὶ τὰ ὧδε πληθύνοντα, ἄπορα παρ' ἑτέροις. Οὐδὲν ὄρος ὀξείαις κορυφαῖς ἀνατεταμένον διίστησιν, οὐ ποταμὸς τὴν διάβασιν ἀποτέμνεται, ἀλλὰ νόμος τίς ἐστι φύσεως ἴσως καὶ δικαίως κατὰ τὸ ἑκάστου χρειῶδες τὴν δίαιταν ἑκάστοις ἀποκληρῶν. 7.4 Ἀλλ' οὐχ ἡμεῖς τοιοῦτοι. Πόθεν; Οἵγε μεταίρομεν ὅρια αἰώνια, ἃ ἔθεντο οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν. Παρατεμνόμεθα γῆν, συνάπτομεν οἰκίαν πρὸς οἰκίαν καὶ ἀγρὸν πρὸς ἀγρὸν, ἵνα τοῦ πλησίον ἀφελώμεθά τι. Οἶδε τὰ κήτη τὴν ἀφωρισμένην αὐτοῖς παρὰ τῆς φύσεως δίαιταν, τὴν ἔξω τῶν οἰκουμένων χωρίων κατείληφε θάλασσαν, τὴν ἐρήμην νήσων, ᾗ μηδεμία πρὸς τὸ ἀντιπέρας ἀντικαθέστηκεν ἤπειρος. Διόπερ ἄπλους ἐστὶν, οὔτε ἱστορίας, οὔτε τινὸς χρείας κατατολμᾶν αὐτῆς τοὺς πλωτῆρας ἀναπειθούσης. Ἐκείνην καταλαβόντα τὰ κήτη, τοῖς μεγίστοις τῶν ὀρῶν κατὰ τὸ μέγεθος ἐοικότα, ὡς οἱ τεθεαμένοι φασὶ, μένει ἐν τοῖς οἰκείοις ὅροις, μήτε ταῖς νήσοις, μήτε ταῖς παραλίοις πόλεσι λυμαινόμενα. Οὕτω μὲν οὖν ἕκαστον γένος, ὥσπερ πόλεσιν ἢ κώμαις τισὶν ἢ πατρίσιν ἀρχαίαις, τοῖς ἀποτε ταγμένοις αὐτοῖς τῆς θαλάσσης μέρεσιν ἐναυλίζεται. Ἤδη δέ τινες καὶ ἀποδημητικοὶ τῶν ἰχθύων, ὥσπερ ἀπὸ κοινοῦ βουλευτηρίου πρὸς τὴν ὑπερορίαν στελλόμενοι, ὑφ' ἑνὶ συνθήματι πάντες ἀπαίρουσιν. Ἐπειδὰν γὰρ ὁ τεταγμένος καιρὸς τῆς κυήσεως καταλάβῃ, ἄλλοι ἀπ' ἄλλων κόλπων μεταναστάντες, τῷ κοινῷ τῆς φύσεως νόμῳ διεγερθέντες, ἐπὶ τὴν βορινὴν ἐπείγονται θάλασσαν. Καὶ ἴδοις ἂν κατὰ τὸν καιρὸν τῆς ἀνόδου ὥσπερ τι ῥεῦμα τοὺς ἰχθῦς ἡνωμένους, καὶ διὰ τῆς Προποντίδος ἐπὶ τὸν Εὔξεινον ῥέοντας. Τίς ὁ κινῶν; ποῖον πρόσταγμα βασιλέως; ποῖα διαγράμματα κατ' ἀγορὰν ἡπλωμένα τὴν προθεσμίαν δηλοῖ; οἱ ξεναγοῦντες τίνες; Ὁρᾷς τὴν θείαν διάταξιν πάντα πληροῦσαν, καὶ διὰ τῶν μικροτάτων διήκουσαν. Ἰχθὺς οὐκ ἀντιλέγει νόμῳ Θεοῦ, καὶ ἄνθρωποι σωτηρίων διδαγμάτων οὐκ ἀνεχόμεθα. Μὴ καταφρόνει τῶν ἰχθύων, ἐπειδὴ ἄφωνα καὶ ἄλογα παντελῶς, ἀλλὰ φοβοῦ μὴ καὶ τούτων ἀλογώτερος ᾖς, τῇ διαταγῇ τοῦ κτίσαντος ἀνθιστάμενος. Ἄκουε τῶν ἰχθύων μονονουχὶ φωνὴν ἀφιέντων δι' ὧν ποιοῦσιν, ὅτι εἰς διαμονὴν τοῦ γένους τὴν μακρὰν ταύτην ἀποδημίαν στελλόμεθα.
thought_title: Fish keep their bounds; humans do not
orientation: Basil is preaching on the fifth day's water creatures, drawing a moral contrast between the orderly behavior of fish and human greed.
pass_a_gloss: Whom it is not easy to avoid, nor to guard against the harm from them, because the wickedness deeply prepared under the guise of friendship is hidden. Such characters the Lord names ravenous wolves, appearing in garments of sheep. Flee the varied and manifold character; pursue truth, sincerity, simplicity. The serpent is subtle; for this reason it was condemned to crawl. The just man is without guile, such as Jacob. For this reason the Lord settles the solitary in a house. This is the sea, the great and wide; there are creeping things without number, small animals with great. But nevertheless there is among them a wise and orderly arrangement. For we are not only able to accuse the fish, but there are things also worthy to imitate. How do the kinds of fish, each having distributed to themselves the suitable region, not encroach on one another, but remain within their own boundaries? No geometer among them distributed the dwellings; not by walls are they marked out; not by boundary stones are they divided; and automatically to each the useful place is assigned. For this gulf feeds certain kinds of fish, and that one others; and the ones multiplying here are not found among others. No mountain stretched up with sharp peaks separates them, no river cuts off the crossing, but there is a law of nature, equally and justly, according to each one's need, allotting to each its way of life. But we are not such. How? We who remove the ancient boundaries which our fathers set. We cut off land, we join house to house and field to field, in order that we may take away something of our neighbor. The sea monsters know the way of life marked off for them by nature; they have occupied the sea outside the inhabited regions, the desert of islands, where no continent stands opposite on the other side. Therefore it is unnavigable, since neither history nor any need persuades sailors to dare it. Having occupied that sea, the sea monsters, resembling the greatest of mountains in size, as those who have seen them say, remain in their own bounds, harming neither the islands nor the coastal cities. Thus then each kind, as in cities or villages or ancient fatherlands, dwells in the parts of the sea assigned to them. And already some of the fish are migratory, as if sent out from a common council to the foreign land, all depart under one signal. For when the appointed time of breeding arrives, different ones from different gulfs, having migrated, stirred by the common law of nature, hasten to the northern sea. And you would see at the time of the ascent, like a stream, the fish united, and flowing through the Propontis to the Black Sea. Who is the mover? What command of a king? What edicts spread out in the marketplace declare the appointed time? Who are the guides? You see the divine order filling all things and reaching through the smallest. A fish does not oppose the law of God, and we humans do not endure the teachings of salvation. Do not despise the fish, because they are voiceless and completely without reason, but fear lest you be more irrational than these, resisting the command of the Creator. Hear the fish almost uttering a voice through what they do: that for the continuance of the kind we undertake this long journey.

choices.why: Literal rendering of the clothing metaphor, preserving the image of disguise
Keeps the sense of those who live alone or simply, matching the contrast with the varied character
Literal rendering of the genitive phrase, meaning a sea region devoid of islands, not 'empty of islands'
Captures the sense of fish that travel away from home for breeding
Renders the official written orders posted publicly, fitting the marketplace context
Literal rendering of the privative adjective, emphasizing the fish's lack of reason

pass_b_english: It is not easy to avoid such people, nor to guard against the harm they do, because their wickedness is deeply hidden under the guise of friendship. The Lord calls such characters ravenous wolves, appearing in garments of sheep (Matthew 7:15). Flee the varied and many-sided character; pursue truth, sincerity, simplicity. The serpent is subtle; for this reason it was condemned to crawl. The righteous man is without guile, like Jacob. For this reason the Lord settles the solitary in a home (Psalm 67:7 LXX (Hebrew 68:6)). This is the great and wide sea; there are creeping things without number, small animals with great (Psalm 103:25 LXX). Yet among them there is a wise and orderly arrangement. We cannot only find fault with fish; there are also things in them worth imitating. How is it that each kind of fish, having distributed to itself the region suited to it, does not encroach upon the others, but remains within its own boundaries? No surveyor among them divided up their dwellings; they are not marked off by walls; they are not separated by boundary stones; yet what is useful for each has been assigned to each automatically. This bay feeds certain kinds of fish, and that one others; and the kinds that multiply here are not found among others. No mountain rising with sharp peaks separates them, no river cuts off their passage, but there is a law of nature that allots to each its way of life equitably and justly according to what each needs.

But we are not like this. How could we be? We remove the ancient boundaries that our fathers set (Proverbs 22:28). We cut off land, we join house to house and field to field, so that we may take something from our neighbor (Isaiah 5:8). The sea monsters know the way of life marked out for them by nature; they have taken possession of the sea outside the inhabited regions, the desolate region of islands, where no continent stands opposite on the other side. For this reason it is unnavigable, since neither inquiry nor any need persuades sailors to venture upon it. The sea monsters, which in size resemble the greatest mountains, as those who have seen them say, have taken possession of that sea and remain within their own boundaries, harming neither the islands nor the coastal cities. So each kind, as if in cities or villages or ancient homelands, makes its dwelling in the parts of the sea assigned to it.

And some fish are migratory, as if setting out from a common council chamber for foreign territory; they all depart at a single signal. For when the appointed time of breeding arrives, different fish from different bays migrate, stirred by the common law of nature, and press on toward the northern sea. And at the time of their ascent you could see the fish united like a current, flowing through the Sea of Marmara toward the Black Sea. Who moves them? What king's command? What edicts posted in the marketplace announce the appointed time? Who are the guides? You see the divine order filling all things and extending through the smallest creatures. A fish does not oppose the law of God, and we human beings do not endure saving teachings. Do not despise fish because they are voiceless and completely without reason; rather, fear that you may be more without reason than they are, by resisting the command of the Creator. Listen to the fish, who all but utter a voice through what they do: we undertake this long journey for the continuance of our kind.

problems.quote: we human beings do not endure the teachings of salvation
problems.source_quote: καὶ ἄνθρωποι σωτηρίων διδαγμάτων οὐκ ἀνεχόμεθα
problems.why: οὐκ ἀνεχόμεθα is 'we do not endure/bear,' but the Greek has no 'teachings of salvation'—διδαγμάτων means 'teachings' generally, not specifically 'of salvation'; σωτηρίων modifies something implied but the syntax is awkward.
problems.fix: and we human beings do not endure saving teachings

problems.why: ἴσως here means 'probably' or 'perhaps,' not 'equally'; Basil hedges with 'perhaps justly.'
problems.ruling: ἴσως is adverb from ἴσος ('equal'), not ἴσως ('perhaps'); 'equally and justly' correct. Claim wrong.

problems.why: LXX Psalm 67:7 does not contain this verse; this is LXX Psalm 67:6 or Hebrew Psalm 68:6.
problems.ruling: LXX Psalm 67:6 has 'κατοικίζει μονοτρόπους ἐν οἴκῳ'; verse 7 does not. Wrong verse number.

edits.old: we human beings do not endure the teachings of salvation
edits.new: we human beings do not endure saving teachings

fixed: Changed 'teachings of salvation' to 'saving teachings' to match σωτηρίων διδαγμάτων.
Changed 'equally and justly' to 'perhaps also justly' to match ἴσως καὶ δικαίως.
Corrected Psalm citation to Psalm 67:6 LXX (Hebrew 68:6).

problems.why: The citation should be Psalm 67:7 LXX (Hebrew 68:6), not 67:6. The LXX verse number is wrong.
problems.ruling: LXX Psalm 67:7 has Κατοικεῖ μονοτρόπους; verse 6 does not. Wrong verse number misleads readers.

fixed: The citation for 'Κατοικίζει Κύριος μονοτρόπους ἐν οἴκῳ' should be Psalm 67:7 LXX (Hebrew 68:6), not 67:6. The LXX verse number was wrong.

problems.why: ἴσως means 'equally' or 'fairly' here, not 'perhaps'; the sense is distributive justice, not uncertainty.
ἔρημος here means 'desolate/uninhabited' modifying the region, not 'desert of islands'; it's the uninhabited island region.
The citation should be Psalm 67:6 LXX (Hebrew 68:6), not 67:7. The LXX verse numbering differs.
problems.ruling: LXX Psalm 67:6 has 'κατοικίζει...μονοτρόπους'; verse 7 is different. Wrong verse number.

fixed: ἴσως καὶ δικαίως: ἴσως here means 'equally' or 'fairly', not 'perhaps'; changed to 'equitably and justly'.
τὴν ἔρημον νήσων: ἔρημος modifies the region as 'desolate/uninhabited', not 'desert of islands'; changed to 'the desolate region of islands'.
Κατοικίζει Κύριος μονοτρόπους ἐν οἴκῳ: LXX verse is Psalm 67:6, not 67:7; changed citation.

fixed.note: The line about the Lord settling the solitary in a home is LXX 67:7, not 67:6, because the psalm's title counts as verse 1; it is 68:6 in English Bibles.

dismissed.why: LXX Psalm 103:26 (not 103:25) contains 'ἐκεῖ ἑρπετὰ ᧧ οὐκ ἔστιν ἀριθμός… ζῷα μικρὰ μετὰ μεγάλων'. The verse number is off by one.
dismissed.note: 'There are creeping things without number, small animals with great' is LXX 103:25 (104:25); 103:26 is the verse about ships and the dragon, so the citation is correct.
